Hi Liam / Priya — technical notes below. I'll keep it high level but flag where the order form needs explicit language.

Background: Redwood's runtime separates ephemeral inference KV (in-memory) from persisted customer objects and logs. Persisted items are written to region-scoped object storage (customer-aware buckets). We take periodic snapshots for faster warm starts and for disaster recovery.

Options for Mediforce (trade-offs listed):

Option A — Standard aligned windows (recommended for cost predictability):
- Primary retention: 30 days
- Snapshot retention: 90 days (snapshots rotated/overwritten; final deletion depends on retention schedule)
- Deletion process: upon contract termination we mark the tenant for deletion, purge primary objects within 24–72 hours, schedule object-store lifecycle to delete snapshots per retention window. We provide a certificate of deletion once the purge job completes and object-store confirms deletions (can take up to 10 business days for snapshot removal depending on provider finalization).
- Impact: lower cost, standard SLA, deletion certificate provided post-process.

Option B — Accelerated residency + certified wipe (premium):
- Primary retention: configurable (e.g., 7/30 days)
- Snapshot retention: reduced to match primary (e.g., 7/30 days) and immediate snapshot immolation workflow triggered on termination.
- Deletion SLA: committed 72-hour deletion window for primary + snapshot objects; includes a signed deletion certificate and a log of object-store delete confirmations.
- Impact: requires dedicated wipe orchestration, potential extra fee, and a short maintenance window to ensure no in-flight writeflows; recommended for regulated customers with short retention needs.

Notes for order form language:
- "Region lock": specify eu-west-1 for all primary objects and a clause that backups and snapshots will not be copied outside eu-west-1 without prior written consent.
- "Certified deletion": Redwood will provide a signed deletion certificate with list of object prefixes and delete confirmation IDs.
- "Exclusions": ephemeral in-memory KV caches are ephemeral by design and not material to data residency; logs that include aggregated telemetry will be redacted per policy but retained for X days (we can set this).

Attached: Draft_SLA_amendment_v2.pdf (contains sample clause wording and pricing delta for accelerated wipe).

Happy to jump on a short call to walk through.
